input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='src/chat_input.rs'; s=open(p).read()
a='''        // What the selected tab is for, in the rest of the bar.
        let help = gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support(
            div()
                .id("tab-help")
                .flex_1()
                .min_w_0()
                .px_3()
                .truncate()
                .text_sm()
                .text_color(cx.theme().muted_foreground)'''
b='''        // What the selected tab is for, in the rest of the bar: smaller and
        // fainter than the tab labels, so it reads as a note about the tab
        // rather than another tab.
        let help = gpui_kit::TestSupportExt::test_support(
            div()
                .id("tab-help")
                .flex_1()
                .min_w_0()
                .px_4()
                .truncate()
                .text_xs()
                .text_color(cx.theme().muted_foreground.opacity(0.7))'''
assert s.count(a)==1; s=s.replace(a,b); open(p,'w').write(s)
p='spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi'; s=open(p).read()
a='''            To the right of the tabs, filling the rest of the bar, a line of
            small, muted help text says what the selected tab is for, and
            changes as soon as another tab is selected. It is cut off rather
            than wrapped when the bar is too narrow.'''
b='''            To the right of the tabs, filling the rest of the bar, a line of
            help text says what the selected tab is for, and changes as soon as
            another tab is selected. It is extra small and dimmer than muted
            text, set a little apart from the last tab, so it reads as a quiet
            note about the tab rather than as another tab. It is cut off rather
            than wrapped when the bar is too narrow.'''
assert s.count(a)==1; s=s.replace(a,b); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cargo test --offline chat_input 2>&1 | grep -E "^error|test result"; piton check spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi | tail -1

content.text:
I made the help text beside the chat input's tabs smaller and dimmer, so it should read as a note rather than another tab. The chat input tests all pass, including the help text test, and the spec checks out. I haven't looked at it in the running app, so check it isn't now too faint to read.

- **Size:** extra small, down one step from small.
- **Colour:** the muted text colour at 70% strength, so a little fainter than other muted text.
- **Spacing:** slightly more gap between it and the Ask tab.

If it needs to go further, italics is the next lever.

The change is in `src/chat_input.rs`, and the help section of `ChatInputScope` now describes the smaller, dimmer style.
